opportunities.title: Dark Sun's Back — Here's the 5e Ruling on Defiling Everyone Forgets
opportunities.why_now: Original Dark Sun creators just announced a 5e conversion of Dragon Kings, reviving interest in defiler/preserver magic mechanics that don't map cleanly to 5e's spell system.
opportunities.angle: 60-sec ruling: how to houserule defiling (temp HP drain to terrain, area-of-effect blight) using existing 5e frameworks, tagged to the announcement.

opportunities.title: An AI Can't Make This Call: Opportunity Attacks in Dim Light
opportunities.why_now: Monte Cook Games' AI-asset controversy is the industry's hot debate this week, giving a natural wry hook to contrast real GM rulings against AI 'good enough' answers.
opportunities.angle: Dry cold-open: 'AI generated my promo video. It still can't rule on this.' Then deliver an actual dim-light/stealth attack ruling using RAW.

opportunities.title: Long Rest Tavern Is Cozy. Your Long Rest Rules Interruption Isn't.
opportunities.why_now: D&D's new cozy tavern-sim game trends on the exact mechanic GMs argue about most: what breaks a long rest.
opportunities.angle: Use the game announcement as clickbait framing, then deliver the actual RAW ruling on interrupted long rests (1hr combat resets the clock, spell slot recovery timing).

opportunities.title: Your Table Got Older. Your Funnel Should Get Meaner.
opportunities.why_now: Gnome Stew's piece on aging tables is fresh and taps into a real GM pain point about pacing/lethality shifts as players' lives change.
opportunities.angle: DCC-specific tactic: adjust funnel lethality and session length for time-crunched veteran tables — practical GM advice, no fluff.

opportunities.title: Shadowdark Ruling: Torches Don't Care About Your Cozy Tavern Vibes
opportunities.why_now: Piggybacks on the cozy-tavern-sim trend to contrast Shadowdark's harsh light/resource economy, a signature differentiator of the system.
opportunities.angle: Quick mechanical breakdown of Shadowdark's real-time torch tracking vs 5e's abstracted light rules, framed as a genre-clash gag.
